label: USE CASE 06
title: How a Bank Support Bot Works

scenes.text: You message your bank's app at midnight, asking why your card was declined. [1] And a bot replies instantly, with the actual reason. [2] Let's break down how a bank's support bot works.

Here's what happens behind that reply. [1] You ask, why was my card declined? [2] First, the bot confirms who you are, safely, through the app's login. [3] It searches the bank's policy documents, and that's RAG. [4] It calls tools to check your actual account, like recent transactions. [5] And it answers, your card hit its daily limit, and you can raise it in settings.

data.heading: Behind the reply
nodes: “Daily limit reached, raise it in settings”

scenes.text: So it's really three ideas working together. [1] RAG, to answer from the bank's own rules and FAQs. [2] Tools, to look up your real account data. [3] And an agent loop, to decide which one to use, and in what order.

Let's see it live. [1] You ask, why was my card declined? [2] The bot calls a tool, get recent transactions, for your card. [3] The bank's system replies, declined, because the daily limit was reached. [4] And the bot explains, and tells you exactly how to raise the limit.

data.heading: The bot, with tools
data.question: Why was my card declined?
data.answer: Your card reached its ₹50,000 daily limit. You can raise it in Settings, under Card limits.

scenes.text: And banks add strong safety rails. [1] Verification, so it only shows your data after you log in. [2] No secrets, so it never asks for your PIN, OTP or password. [3] Limits, so it can't move money without your confirmation. [4] And human handoff, so complaints and fraud cases go to a real person.

So where will you see this? [1] Banking apps answering card and account questions. [2] Telecom apps handling plan changes and bill queries. [3] And airline apps rebooking your flight when there's a delay.

Here's a common myth. [1] People think a support bot can do anything a bank employee can. [2] It can't, and that's by design. It only gets specific tools and permissions, and anything risky goes to a human. And remember, no real bank bot will ever ask for your OTP.

data.myth: A support bot can do anything a bank employee can.
data.fact: It only gets specific tools and permissions. Anything risky goes to a human.

scenes.text: Let's recap. [1] RAG lets the bot answer from the bank's rules. [2] Tools let it check your real account. [3] An agent loop decides what to do next.
